passage:
Harish, come, sit. I will tell you about my worst family group. I was twenty-one, Sarika to everyone, and I loved sending things. Forty good-morning pictures, jokes, prayers, all before breakfast, in our big cousins' group.
One day Harish's father, my cousin, said, "Sarika, I muted the group months ago. I only found out the wedding hall had changed from a neighbour."
I went cold. I asked the others, and half of them had muted it too. My forwards had hidden the one message that mattered.
After that I sent one message a day, and used the group only for real news. Quiet people began to answer again.

qa.q: How many good-morning pictures and jokes did Sarika send before breakfast?
qa.a: Sarika sent forty good-morning pictures, jokes and prayers before breakfast.

qa.q: What was Sarika feeling when told that the group had been muted for months?
qa.a: Sarika felt shocked and ashamed. Going cold on hearing that half the group had muted the chat shows how badly Sarika's forwards had landed.

qa.q: What did Sarika decide after finding out, and what changed in the group?
qa.a: Sarika chose to send one message a day and use the group only for real news. The quiet members began to answer again.

qa.q: How did Harish's father find out that the wedding hall had changed?
qa.a: A neighbour told Harish's father, because the group had been muted for months. The forwards had buried the message, so the news nearly went unseen.

grounding: A young adult floods a family group with forwards, learns members muted it and missed key news, and changes their habit, told by an elder as a memory.

passage:
Twenty-five minutes before the exam, Usha was still forwarding memes into the college batch chat. Sixty since morning, and each one made Usha grin.
Outside the hall, Rafiq scrolled up the muted chat and squinted. Somewhere between a dancing cat and a motivational quote was the notice: Exam room changed to Block C. Rafiq ran across the courtyard, breathless, and slid in as the papers were handed out.
At the tea stall afterwards Rafiq said, "I nearly missed the room. That notice was under forty forwards."
Usha's grin faded. That night Usha posted one line only: "Notices here from now. Memes in a separate chat."

qa.q: Which block was the exam room changed to?
qa.a: The exam room was changed to Block C.

qa.q: What was Usha feeling as the memes were sent, and how did it change after the tea stall?
qa.a: Usha was cheerful and playful while forwarding memes. After Rafiq's remark Usha felt guilty and sobered, and the grin faded.

qa.q: What did Usha decide to do differently that night?
qa.a: Usha posted one line saying notices only would go in the main chat and memes would move to a separate chat. That keeps important information easy to find.

qa.q: What was it like for Rafiq to find the room notice?
qa.a: Rafiq was rushed and stressed, scrolling a muted chat and running across the courtyard to get to the exam in time. The important notice was buried under forty forwards.

grounding: A college member floods the batch chat with memes and forwards, a quiet member almost misses an exam room change, and the flooder changes course.

passage:
Thursday, hostel room 12
Today Irawati asked me, at the mess, why nobody told her about the practical exam being shifted to Lab 3. I said, "I posted it in the group!" She looked embarrassed and said, "Sudha, I muted the group two weeks ago. There were like eighty messages a day."
Eighty. I counted mine from yesterday: good morning flower, two jokes, a video of a baby elephant, a quote about success, four forwards about exam tips, a sunset I took from the terrace. Sixteen, just from me.
I thought I was keeping the group alive. I thought everyone liked the elephant.
Irawati said three more girls have muted it too. And the room-change notice got buried under my sunset.
I felt my ears go hot at the mess table.
New rule for me: one fun thing a day, maximum. Important notices pinned. The elephant can go to my cousins.

qa.q: How many messages did Sudha post the day before?
qa.a: Sudha counted sixteen, just from Sudha.

qa.q: What was Sudha feeling when Irawati explained why she had muted the group?
qa.a: Sudha felt embarrassed and a little hurt, with ears going hot, since the forwards were meant to keep the group alive.

qa.q: What new rule did Sudha set, and why might it help?
qa.a: One fun thing a day and important notices pinned, so the group stays useful and members stop muting it.

qa.q: How did the flood of forwards affect Irawati?
qa.a: Irawati felt overwhelmed by around eighty messages a day, muted the group, and then missed the practical exam change, which left her anxious and embarrassed.

grounding: A member floods a college group with forwards and good-morning posts, and quiet members mute it and miss important news.

passage:
Alka: Harish, why did nobody come to Nani's small puja on Sunday?? I posted it in the family group!!
Harish: ahh. Alka didi, honestly? most of us have the family group on mute
Alka: MUTE? why
Harish: you posted 43 things yesterday. I counted. flowers, quotes, three videos of cats playing piano
Alka: but everyone likes the good mornings 😢
Harish: some do! Chachi does. but the puja message was between a cat and a recipe
Harish: Papa scrolled and gave up
Alka: I was trying to make the group happy
Harish: I know didi, you're the only one who posts. that's why it's alive
Harish: maybe put the fun stuff in a separate "masti" group? and keep family group for real things
Alka: fine. but you have to join masti
Harish: 🙏 I'll join. muted, but I'll join
Alka: HARISH
Harish: joking!!

qa.q: How many things did Alka post the day before, according to Harish?
qa.a: Harish says Alka posted 43 things yesterday.

qa.q: What was Alka feeling when she learned people had muted the group?
qa.a: Alka felt hurt and disappointed, since she had been posting to make the group happy, and upset that nobody came to Nani's puja.

qa.q: What kind, specific idea did Harish offer?
qa.a: Keep the family group for real things and move the fun posts to a separate "masti" group.

qa.q: How does Harish see Alka's posting?
qa.a: Harish is fond of Alka and knows her posts keep the group alive, but finds the flood overwhelming and understands why others muted it.

grounding: A member floods a family group with forwards, many relatives mute it, and they miss the important puja message.

passage:
Lakshmi was the class representative at the polytechnic in their small town, and she took the job seriously. Every morning she posted a sunrise image with "Suprabhat, friends!" Then a quote, then a funny video, then two news forwards, then a photo of the canteen's fresh jalebis.
On Friday, Nirmala came running into the workshop, breathless and late. "Why did no one tell me the practical moved to eight?"
"I posted it last night!" Lakshmi said.
Nirmala pulled out her phone. The notice was there, somewhere between a video of a dancing parrot and a flower gif. The group icon showed a small crossed-out bell. "Lakshmi, I muted it last month. It buzzed through my whole bus ride."
Lakshmi looked at the list of members. Only four had seen the notice.
That evening she posted one message: "From now on, only class info here. Fun stuff in a separate group, join if you like."

qa.q: What did Lakshmi post every morning?
qa.a: Every morning she posted a sunrise image with "Suprabhat, friends!"

qa.q: What was Nirmala feeling when she came into the workshop?
qa.a: She came running in breathless and late, and her question to Lakshmi shows she was anxious and frustrated about missing the time change.

qa.q: Which choice worked, and why?
qa.a: Lakshmi separated class information from fun posts, so important notices will no longer be buried and members may unmute.

qa.q: What would change if Lakshmi kept posting the same way?
qa.a: More classmates would likely mute the group and miss notices, and Lakshmi's role as class representative would lose its point.

grounding: A member floods a college group with good-morning posts and forwards, and a quiet member who muted it misses important news.

passage: Every morning at six, before the first bus left for campus in Addis Ababa, Abebe opened the class group and started posting: a sunrise with "Good morning, champions!", a forwarded video of a dancing goat, three motivational quotes, a meme about exams. By lunch he had usually sent twenty or thirty things. He liked imagining everyone smiling at them. On Tuesday the lecturer posted one line: the statistics mid-term had moved to Hall B. Within the hour it sank under goats and quotes. On Wednesday Liam, the exchange student from Dublin, turned up at Hall A alone and ran across campus, arriving eleven minutes late. "Sorry," he told Abebe afterwards, "I muted the group in week two. Too much to scroll." Abebe checked: fourteen of the forty members had muted it. That evening he started a separate group called "Abebe's morning stuff" and invited anyone who wanted it. Six people joined.

qa.q: Where had the statistics mid-term moved?
qa.a: The statistics mid-term had moved to Hall B.

qa.q: What might Abebe have felt on learning that fourteen members had muted the group?
qa.a: He probably felt a sting of embarrassment and some guilt, since he meant to make people smile but had helped bury the hall change.

qa.q: What did the new group fix, and what else could help?
qa.a: It kept Abebe's cheerful posts for the people who wanted them, so class notices stay visible; pinning important messages would also help.

qa.q: What was Wednesday like for Liam?
qa.a: Having muted the flood, Liam missed the notice, found himself alone in Hall A and had to run, arriving eleven minutes late and flustered.

grounding: Shows a member filling a college group with forwards and good-morning posts until quiet members mute it and miss an important notice.
